notes: Text fields and dropdowns look calmer in Dark mode.
The first update that comes straight from the catalog, without a new Tavora version.
A ⚙ menu in the toolbar: pick how many decimal places results show, and how many results the history keeps (10, 25 or 50).
Short numbers: results from a million on can show as 1.5M, 2B or 3T.
Copy and your sums always use the full number.
Save as… keeps a result under a name, like iron. Tap it under Values to use it in a sum.
A sum counts with the value as it is now; if you delete it, the sum tells you.
Plus has a new row: k, m and b for thousands, millions and billions, and ⌈x⌉ to round up. You can type k, m and b in Basic too.
Enter works on the key you tabbed to, instead of acting on the sum.
Clear history asks first.
Only the result line is read out loud, not every key.
The keys keep a size you can press, in small panels too; a short panel scrolls instead.
The history keeps room for your results below or beside the keypad.
A toolbar on top: switch between the Basic keypad and Plus, and show or hide your history.
The keypad no longer gets cut off when the panel is wide but not wide enough for the history beside it.
New keys: √, x², ± and ans for your last result, with the Windows shortcuts @, q and F9.
Copy puts the result on your clipboard as a plain number, also with Ctrl+C.
Big numbers show their thousands, like 1,234,567.
A quick calculator for each game, with your keyboard too.
Your last 10 results stay, so you can pick them up again.
